content.text: Proposed outline for comment from sprinters and stakeholders:
Briefly introduce the Import-Export efforts
Show the tool in GitHub - README, and Confluence documentation?
Demonstrate a basic export
Demonstrate a basic import
Demonstrate a basic export to a bag
Each video should have a transcript for accessibility and captions.  I suggest max 1 min videos if at all possible.
Briefly introduce the Import-Export efforts  – is this a marketing video or technical video?
Show the tool in GitHub - README, and Confluence documentation? - no video necessary
Demonstrate a basic export
Demonstrate a basic import
Demonstrate a basic export to a bag

3-5:  may be make the best videos if one can point to/highlights in addition to screen capture of actions. Suggest at minimum of 10 items for demo.  IT would be good to break up videos on importing on a set vs. repo and including videos to check that import / export worked successfully as separate videos.
Do we know if most users have PCs or Macs for demoing in video?
Starting with 3-5 sounds like a good approach.
The document linked below is a draft proposal for a video campaign:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1CzvJlZ3m3eEhHgVJJY0hdGerPMxRIRaK9X05WhCLKpo/edit?usp=sharing
The content of your proposal,
, is intriguing. Do you envision having additional videos along the lines of
's comment above from 15/Dec/16? i.e. "How to videos"?
Yes,

's comment should probably be addressed first. I am not sure it could be done in one minute, but for this first introductory video, two sprint participants could use screen sharing in Google Hangouts to demonstrate export and verification (participant A), upload/download, then import and verification (participant B). The recorded conversation could be edited and a small sample data set could be used to speed things up.

This task is to define the content of a few short (3 minutes?) videos that will demonstrate how to use the import/export tooling. Ideally, these can be used to engage more of the community in verifying the tools.
This ticket will be complete when new JIRA tickets have been created that detail the specifics of each of the videos that will be created in Sprint 3.

Proposed outline for comment from sprinters and stakeholders:

  1. Briefly introduce the Import-Export efforts
  2. Show the tool in GitHub - README, and Confluence documentation?
  3. Demonstrate a basic export
  4. Demonstrate a basic import
  5. Demonstrate a basic export to a bag

Each video should have a transcript for accessibility and captions. I suggest max 1 min videos if at all possible.

  1. Briefly introduce the Import-Export efforts – is this a marketing video or technical video?
  2. Show the tool in GitHub - README, and Confluence documentation? - no video necessary
  3. Demonstrate a basic export
  4. Demonstrate a basic import
  5. Demonstrate a basic export to a bag

3-5: may be make the best videos if one can point to/highlights in addition to screen capture of actions. Suggest at minimum of 10 items for demo. IT would be good to break up videos on importing on a set vs. repo and including videos to check that import / export worked successfully as separate videos.

Do we know if most users have PCs or Macs for demoing in video?
Starting with 3-5 sounds like a good approach.

The document linked below is a draft proposal for a video campaign:
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1CzvJlZ3m3eEhHgVJJY0hdGerPMxRIRaK9X05WhCLKpo/edit?usp=sharing
The content of your proposal, Youn Noh, is intriguing. Do you envision having additional videos along the lines of kestlund's comment above from 15/Dec/16? i.e. "How to videos"?

Yes, kestlund's comment should probably be addressed first. I am not sure it could be done in one minute, but for this first introductory video, two sprint participants could use screen sharing in Google Hangouts to demonstrate export and verification (participant A), upload/download, then import and verification (participant B). The recorded conversation could be edited and a small sample data set could be used to speed things up.
